verdict.rationale: Orama documents on-premise deployment of Orama Cloud's context server on your own infrastructure, and says it runs in your cloud, on-prem, or dedicated. Separately, it ships an open-source library whose APIs are 'as close as possible' to Cloud. However, nothing confirms the self-hosted deployment matches the hosted product feature-for-feature, and the OSS AnswerSession still relies on Orama Cloud's Secure Proxy. missing for 10: documented feature parity between on-prem and hosted Cloud, self-hosting deployment/operations docs, independent or hands-on corroboration of on-prem deployments.

support.subject: As a platform-engineer, I can self-host the full engine — same features as the hosted product — on my own infrastructure

citations.quote: We offer on-premise support for Orama Cloud, allowing you to deploy the context server on your own infrastructure.
It runs in your cloud, on-prem, or dedicated, and our forward-deployed engineers run it with your team.
The APIs are designed to be as close as possible to the **Orama Cloud** APIs, so you can easily migrate your projects from **Orama Cloud** to **Orama Open Source** and vice-versa.
